scope.status: not a PDP decision (only its origin-kind outcome is)
scope.where: verifier.py ingest stages 2-3: UNKNOWN_KEY, KEY_SUBJECT_MISMATCH, KEY_KIND_INVALID, INTEGRITY_RELAY, BINDING_MISMATCH, INTEGRITY_OBS (identity.py TrustView/TrustRegistry; crypto.verify)
scope.covered_here: The PDP only receives origin_kind, derived from the verified key kind ('device'|'workload'). Origin-kind combinations are tested (category origin_kind_mismatch and the grid).

scope.where: verifier.py ingest stage 4: KEY_NOT_YET_VALID, KEY_EXPIRED (quarantine), KEY_IN_GRACE annotation (params.rotation_grace_ms is read from the policy document but applied by the verifier)
scope.covered_here: nothing (no PDP input carries validity times)

scope.where: verifier.py ingest stage 4 and _apply_taints: REVOKED, REVOKED_BUFFERED (quarantine), taint propagation (identity.py TrustView.status)
scope.covered_here: nothing. Deactivating a device/workload in the policy document ('active': false) IS a PDP decision and is tested (inactive_device, inactive_workload), but it is not credential revocation.

scope.where: PDP: legacy devices carry origin requirement 'gateway' (the edge workload may sign for them). Aged/buffered legacy data is a freshness decision in verifier.py (STALE_TS, FUTURE_TS, STALE_EPOCH).
scope.covered_here: gateway-origin (legacy) devices with every origin kind (grid + origin_kind_mismatch); data age is out of scope

scope.status: PDP-level only; unreachable through the PBTI verifier
scope.where: envelope.pbti_parse rejects missing/empty/non-string did, aid, sch, wid as MALFORMED before the PDP; origin_kind is computed by the verifier

scope.status: PDP-level only; unreachable through the PBTI verifier
scope.covered_here: wrong_types, empty_strings; plus malformed_policy_document (both evaluators validate the policy document: the Python PolicyStore refuses a schema-violating document at load time, the Rego policy denies with POLICY_DOCUMENT_INVALID)

scope.where: verifier.py: QUARANTINE dispositions (FUTURE_TS, STALE_TS, KEY_EXPIRED, REVOKED_BUFFERED, STALE_SLOT, STALE_EPOCH, SEQ_JUMP) and later re-delivery; the PDP returns only permit/deny
scope.covered_here: only policy-level recovery: version v5 re-activates the device and workload deactivated in v3/v4; decisions under v5 are compared with v2

scope.where: PDP: unknown did -> DEVICE_NOT_REGISTERED, unknown wid -> WORKLOAD_NOT_REGISTERED. Unknown keys (UNKNOWN_KEY) are rejected by the verifier before the PDP.

PDP: the only time dependence is policy-version selection (PDP.active_version: latest version with t_ms <= t; earliest version if none). Skew (skew_max_ms), horizon (h_max_ms), retry window, epoch drain and rotation grace are verifier checks.
scope.covered_here: version_selection_clock_boundary (t_k-1, t_k, t_k+1 for every version change; t<0; far future). Rego has no time input: version selection is the integrator's job, so only the Python selection is tested and Rego is evaluated on the version in force.
